decision: A fresh canonical KDE window observation, bounded by existing 20ms I/O budget, plus actual /proc PID executable chrome selects a 100ms compatibility activation deadline. All existing ordered Get/nonce/marker/request/revocation/expiry/Ready checks are reused. Missing observation, another executable or non-KDE selects the original default. No retries, extra wakeup, queue, cached proof or edit authority. Begin the existing activation request synchronously before any platform timing future is polled. Select the Chrome deadline inside that same acquisition worker; no extra worker or request owner. This preserves the exact PendingLiteral receipt for the first key during classification.
tradeoff: KDE compatibility focus now performs one bounded canonical-window timing classification; only actual Chrome receives the longer admission budget. This is not an unconditional 100ms wait. Other KDE clients retain their deadline but additional focus-probe latency is not physically certified by this Chrome-only work. Canonical KWin classification is synchronous, bounded by the existing 20ms deadline, and executes in the existing worker; it can occupy the connection executor for that bounded period. No sleep, retry or longer unbounded classification is introduced.
